card_title: How to Turn On Claude Meetings
card_desc: Who has it, how to add Claude to a Google Meet call, what to ask it while you talk, and what you get after.
meta_title: How to Turn On Claude Meetings (and What to Ask It) | Olivia Porter
meta_description: Claude Meetings is in beta on Claude Team and Enterprise plans and joins Google Meet calls. Here's how to turn it on, what to ask it during a call, and where to find the notes after.
sub: Claude can join your Google Meet calls. Here's who has it, how to add it, what to ask it, and what you get after.
intro: Here's the scoop on Claude Meetings.
It's in beta and only on some plans. Not on one of them? Skip to the end. There's a version that works for everyone.

before.label: Who has it
items: Claude Meetings is in beta on Claude Team and Enterprise plans, in Claude and the Claude desktop app. It works with Google Meet.
On Team plans it's on by default and an owner can turn it off. On Enterprise plans, an owner turns it on for all or part of the organization.

By default Claude stays out of calls with people outside your company, and leaves if one joins partway through. If an owner allows outside guests, Claude takes notes but doesn't reply in the call's chat, and guests don't get the notes.
Some setups can't use it yet.
During the beta it isn't available to some organizations, including those set up for zero data retention, HIPAA, or customer-managed encryption keys.

steps.title: Open Meetings in Claude
steps.text: In Claude or the Claude desktop app, go to Meetings, or go straight to claude.ai/meetings.

steps.title: Connect Google Calendar
steps.text: Connect your Google Calendar so Claude can see your meetings. An owner may need to allow Google Calendar for your organization first.

steps.title: Get everyone's OK first
steps.text: Before you add Claude, make sure everyone on the call is okay with being transcribed. Add a line to the invite, like: “Heads up: I'll have Claude join our call to take notes. Let me know if you'd rather it didn't.”

steps.title: Add Claude to the meeting
steps.text: Pick the meeting and click Add Claude. Claude joins the Google Meet call as a participant, posts a notice in the call's chat, and shows a live tile with what it's doing. It can stay up to 8 hours and warns you before it leaves.

steps.title: Optional: have it join on its own
steps.text: Go to Settings > Capabilities > Meetings > Auto-join. Choose all your meetings, or all your meetings except one-on-ones.

steps.title: How to ask
steps.text: Say “Claude” and ask your question out loud, or type it in the Meet chat. It answers in the Meet chat, and everyone on the call can see what it posts.

steps.title: Check what's agreed
steps.text: Halfway through, or near the end, ask:
steps.prompt: Summarize what we agreed so far.

steps.title: Get the action items
steps.prompt: List the action items with owners.

steps.title: Turn it into a plan
steps.prompt: Turn this into a one page plan.

steps.title: Pause it or take it out
steps.text: Ask Claude to stop listening, or use the meeting page. To take it out of the call, click Remove Claude on the meeting page.

steps.title: Find the notes
steps.text: Open the meeting in Meetings. You'll find the notes (a summary and any action items), the transcript, and anything Claude made during the call. People from your company who were on the invite get a recap email with a link. Claude keeps the transcript, summary and screen descriptions, not the audio.

steps.title: Ask about it later
steps.text: In any regular Claude chat, you can ask about past meetings you have access to. Try:
steps.prompt: What did we agree on in my last call with [name], and what's still open?

steps.title: Send the follow-up
steps.text: Paste the summary into my follow-up email prompt to get a short follow-up with next steps, owners and dates.

steps.title: Use any notetaker and my follow-up prompt
steps.text: Claude Meetings needs a Claude Team or Enterprise plan. On any other plan, take the summary from whatever notetaker you use, or your own quick notes, and paste it into Claude or ChatGPT with my follow-up email prompt.

closing: It's a beta, so details can change. Claude's help article has the latest.
